title: Ops Lens: Dashboard choreography + Metric sanity checks
summary: Working notes for a compact incident-first dashboard choreography and a short checklist of metric sanity checks + cheap query cost estimates for common investigative paths.
body:
Purpose:
Quick-reference doc for oncall and SREs to: 1) follow a predictable panel order (choreography) during token-serving incidents, 2) validate metric health (sanity checks) before deep dives, and 3) choose cost-aware queries and trace sampling knobs to minimize billing/latency impact while still getting signal.

Audience:
- Oncall operator starting an investigation
- Observability instrumenter making lightweight metric/trace choices
- Eng leads preparing compact dashboards for rotations

1) Dashboard choreography (panel order) — why this helps
- Goal: reduce investigator scatter by always visiting the same ordered set of panels. Panels are grouped by fastest-to-know, cheapest-to-run, highest-signal.
- Time budget: aim to surface high-level signal in <= 2 minutes, initial hypotheses in <= 10 minutes.

Panel order (compact):
A. Global ingress & errors (1 panel) — request rate (rps), 5xx rate, throttled count. Quick check: is traffic spike or error spike?
B. Latency at quantiles (p50/p95/p99) per route/model (1 heatmap) — check if latency is widespread or cohorted.
C. KV cache warmth + hit rate (1 panel) — distinguishes cold-cache evictions vs runtime slowdown.
D. Queue depth / backpressure (1 panel) — queueing indicates saturation, not pure compute regression.
E. Model variant routing & fallback counts (1 panel) — did routing change to fallbacks?
F. Per-tenant token cost spike (sampled) + tenant error ribbon (1 panel) — check noisy tenant.
G. Trace anchors (1 panel) — top trace entry points by count and by error score. Use low-cardinality anchors first.
H. Recent sampled traces list (links) — allow one-click jump into trace viewer.
I. Worker/GPU utilization + OOMs (1 panel) — hardware-level saturation.
J. Deployment/rollout events feed (1 panel) — recent model/version/infra events.

Notes on panels: keep each to a single query or pre-aggregated metric to avoid large ad-hoc scans. Prefer precomputed rollups for p99 where available.

2) Metric sanity checklist (do these before enumerating hypotheses)
- Freshness: are metric timestamps <= 60s behind? If not, note telemetry pipeline lag.
- Aggregation sanity: are units consistent (tokens/s vs requests/s)? Check units in panel title.
- Cardinality blowups: did a label cardinality increase (tenant_id, prompt_hash)? Check metric-cardinality delta panel.
- Sample-rate awareness: are traces/latency panels already sampled? If trace sampling is aggressive, increase only for the suspected timeframe.
- Alert context: check alert firing history window (last 30m) to avoid chasing flapping alerts.
- Baseline drift: compare same-hour-of-week baseline for last 4 weeks for p95/p99 — quick sanity for seasonal traffic.

3) Trace sampling heuristics (cheap, targeted increases)
- Default: session-level adaptive sampling at 1–2% for steady traffic.
- Spike/incident mode: bump to 5% but only for routes with p95 > threshold or for tenant ids with > X 5xxs.
- Error-first: sample 100% of errored requests for 30 minutes for the implicated route.
- Tail-sampling anchors: if p99 unexplained, seed trace collector with top N slow request hashes (N=200) for 10m.
- TTL & cleanup: reset sampling settings to default after 30–60m, create short-lived sampling tickets in JIRA if needed.

4) Cost-aware query playbook (back-of-envelope)
- Rule of thumb: broad ad-hoc traces cost ~10–50x a short pre-aggregated metric query. Prefer metric panels first.
- Low-cost quick queries (good first steps): 
  * 1m-resolution p95 heatmap by route (pre-aggregated) — cheap, yields distribution shape
  * Top 20 tenants by error count in last 5m — cheap if pre-aggregated rollup exists
  * KV hit rate by route (30s rollup) — cheap and high signal
- Higher-cost actions (cost vs value):
  * Full trace capture for route across 15m — moderate cost; do only if metric+heatmap inconclusive
  * Retrospective tail-sampling replay over 1h window — high cost; prefer targeted tail anchors instead

5) Quick investigation checklist (10-minute template)
- 0:00–01:30 — Global ingress & errors. If no anomaly, stop and mark as noise.
- 01:30–03:30 — Latency heatmap + KV warmth. If KV cold or queueing, engage infra.
- 03:30–06:00 — Check routing fallbacks and rollout feed. If rollout correlated, trigger rollback play.
- 06:00–09:00 — Surface traces (sampled) only for implicated route and errored requests.
- 09:00–10:00 — Make hypothesis, page owner, create incident doc, set next cadence.

6) Follow-ups for instrumentation team
- Add a lightweight metric: route_prefixed_request_count (5s rollup) for multi-model fanout paths.
- Ensure p99 rollups are stored at 1m resolution for at least 7 days.
- Add cardinality monitor alert for tenant_id tag growth > 3x day-over-day.
- Add annotation pipeline for rollout events (model/version) to auto-link with timeline.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What threshold should automatically flip sampling to 5%? (proposal: p95 > 2x baseline for 5m)
- Should we enable automated short-lived tail-sampling on p99 decay detection? (ops + infra tradeoff)

References & links:
- Confluence runbook index (linked above)
- Telemetry repo PR for pre-aggregated rollups: linked_artifacts
- Slack channel: #ops-observability (use for oncall broadcast)

Appendix: cheap instrumentation snippets (for engineers)
- PromQL example for 5m rolling p95 per route (pre-agg):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- KV hit rate (30s rollup):
  sum(rate(kv_get_hits_total[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_get_total[1m]))

Tone: intentionally concise; keep this doc short and referee-able. Add to rotation checklist and iterate after two rotations.
